native_mcp_support.notes: Supported via 'Connectors' — registered MCP servers exposed to the model as tools in Conversations, Agents and Vibe Code; Mistral runs the MCP transport server-side, the client does not. Still labelled 'Public Preview — the API interface can change' on the Studio Connectors page (checked 2026-08-19). The 2026-06-24 update added per-tool enable/disable for a whole org or one workspace, connector-scoped API keys, and moved Enterprise controls, Connector Credentials and Connectors-in-Vibe-Code to GA, while Connectors Playground and Connectors in Workflows stay in public preview (https://mistral.ai/news/more-control-over-connectors/). REST surface: GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /v1/connectors plus GET /v1/connectors/{id}/tools (https://docs.mistral.ai/api/endpoint/beta/connectors).

skills_concept.value: Skills — versioned, reusable instruction bundles (title + trigger description + instructions + optional attached files) loaded on demand by description match; plus Agents (pre-configured model instances with instructions and tools) and server-side Conversations
skills_concept.notes: CHANGED since 2026-06-21: Mistral now ships an explicit, first-class 'Skills' primitive (Studio + Vibe), not just Agents. Studio Skills are immutably versioned with rollback, and 'the description field ... determines when the assistant loads the Skill' — i.e. progressive disclosure, not always-on. Vibe Skills are SKILL.md folders discovered name+description-first (~100 tokens each) and expanded on activation (https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/work/skills). Skills are also reachable as MCP servers from Studio (https://mistral.ai/news/manage-prompts-and-skills-in-studio/). Agents remain the API-side construct (https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/agents/introduction).

release_date.notes: Re-verified on the model card 2026-08-19; unchanged.

knowledge_cutoff.notes: Still not published. Checked the Mistral model card (https://docs.mistral.ai/models/model-cards/mistral-medium-3-5-26-04) and the official Hugging Face model card (https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B) on 2026-08-19 — neither states a training-data cutoff date.

context_window_tokens.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19: the Known Limitations context-window table still lists this model at 256k tokens; the official HF model card (https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B) repeats '256k context'.

input_output_shared.notes: Known Limitations, re-read 2026-08-19: both input and output tokens are included in the context calculation — 'Plan your max_tokens accordingly.'

max_input_tokens.notes: No separate input ceiling is published. The chat endpoint reference states only that 'The token count of your prompt plus max_tokens cannot exceed the model's context length', so the effective input ceiling is 256k minus the requested max_tokens. Not recorded as a number because it is request-dependent, not a documented constant.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: No default value for max_tokens is documented on the chat endpoint reference (re-read 2026-08-19); the parameter is described without a stated default or maximum.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: No per-completion output ceiling is published. The only documented bound is 'prompt + max_tokens cannot exceed the model's context length' (256k). This is a genuine documentation gap, not an absence of constraint — the shared 256k window is what binds.

extended_context.notes: No extended/beta context tier beyond 256k appears in the Known Limitations table (re-read 2026-08-19).

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: CHANGED sourcing: this model IS a reasoning model. The Reasoning page lists mistral-medium-3-5 as supporting the per-request reasoning_effort parameter ('high' emits a ThinkChunk before the TextChunk; 'none' omits it); the HF model card (https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B) repeats 'configurable reasoning effort per request'. Mistral does NOT document how thinking tokens are counted or billed, and there is no thinking-budget parameter — so the value stays null rather than assuming they bill as output.

tokenizer_family.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19. Mistral's tokenization deep-dive still documents V1/V2/V3 with V3-Tekken as the tiktoken-based variant used by recent models; the official HF card for this model (https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B) names Tekken and pins a minimum mistral-common version. Exact Tekken sub-version per model is not published.

tokenizer_public.notes: mistral-common remains open source; tokenizer files are downloadable from the HF Hub.

tokenizer_access.value: pip install mistral-common; MistralTokenizer.from_hf_hub("<hf-model-id>") pulls the Tekken tokenizer from the HF Hub
tokenizer_access.notes: Refreshed 2026-08-19 to the current documented loading path. Extras: pip install "mistral-common[image]" / "mistral-common[audio,hf-hub]".

count_tokens_method.value: from mistral_common.tokens.tokenizers.mistral import MistralTokenizer; tok = MistralTokenizer.from_hf_hub("<hf-model-id>"); n = len(tok.encode_chat_completion(ChatCompletionRequest(messages=[...])).tokens)
count_tokens_method.notes: CHANGED: the previously recorded MistralTokenizer.v3() call is superseded by the documented from_hf_hub + encode_chat_completion flow. Caveat verified 2026-08-19: the mistral-common usage docs show no worked example of putting `tools` into the ChatCompletionRequest, so tool-definition token counts obtained this way are reconstructions, not a vendor-blessed recipe. Mistral exposes no server-side count-tokens endpoint.

image_token_rule.notes: Still undocumented, and now confirmed as a deliberate gap: the Vision capability page carries the FAQ heading 'How many tokens correspond to an image and/or what is the maximum resolution?' with no answer beneath it (checked 2026-08-19). The only published image constraint is a 20 MB per-image cap in Known Limitations (https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations).

audio_token_rule.notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-19: the model card does not list audio as a capability for this model, and the official HF card (https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B) gives the modalities as text+image in / text out. Audio is handled by the separate Voxtral models and endpoints, so no audio token rule applies here. (The 2026-06-21 entry's 'audio transcription listed as a feature' claim did not hold up on re-read.)

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: CHANGED to null: the previous 4.0 was an unsourced industry rule of thumb. Searched Mistral's tokenization deep-dive, the mistral-common docs and the Tekken tokenizer card (https://huggingface.co/toksuite/mistralai-tekken, vocab 130,000, tier 3) on 2026-08-19 — no chars-per-token or bytes-per-token figure is published for Tekken. The only quantitative claim Mistral makes is relative: Tekken is '~30% more efficient at compressing source code, Chinese, Italian, French, German, Spanish, and Russian' and 2x/3x on Korean/Arabic versus the Llama 3 tokenizer. Use mistral-common for exact counts.

function_calling.notes: Function Calling is listed in the model card's feature list (re-verified 2026-08-19) and the model appears in the function-calling guide's supported-model list (https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/function_calling).

native_mcp.notes: Platform-level: any function-calling model can be pointed at registered Connectors (MCP servers), whose tools the model 'discovers automatically and calls ... based on the user's request'. Still Public Preview as of 2026-08-19; the API interface can change. Vibe Code additionally speaks MCP directly over stdio, HTTP and streamable HTTP (https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/mcp-servers).

parallel_tool_calls.notes: Re-verified on the chat endpoint reference 2026-08-19: parallel_tool_calls — 'Whether to enable parallel function calling during tool use, when enabled the model can call multiple tools in parallel.' Default Value: true.

max_tools_hard.notes: Unchanged and re-verified 2026-08-19: Known Limitations still states 'Maximum number of tools per request: 128.' SCOPE = AGGREGATE — it counts every tool in the request's `tools` array together: your own functions, every tool pulled in from each connected Connector (MCP server), and Mistral's built-in tools (web search, code interpreter, image generation, document library), which are passed in the same array (https://docs.mistral.ai/api/endpoint/chat). It is not a per-MCP-server cap; no per-server tool cap is documented anywhere.

max_tools_practical.notes: CHANGED 20 → null (2026-08-19 final audit): no empirical source has measured a Mistral model's tool-count degradation, so no practical tool ceiling can be asserted for Mistral Medium 3.5. The previously cited leaderboard (https://presenc.ai/research/ai-agent-tool-calling-accuracy-benchmarks-2026, tier 4, re-opened 2026-08-19) measures only Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-5, Qwen 3 235B, Llama 4 405B, Qwen 3 32B, Llama 4 70B and DeepSeek V4 — NO Mistral model appears in it, so its "accuracy degrades to 85-91 percent at 5 tools, then to 65-78 percent at 20+ tools" band (exemplified on Claude Opus 4.7: 96% at 1 tool → 91% at 5 → 76% at 20+) is evidence about those models only. The practitioner write-up previously quoted alongside it (https://tianpan.co/blog/2026-04-19-over-tooled-agent-problem, "safe zone ... at roughly 10-20 tools per reasoning context") likewise names no Mistral model. Mistral itself publishes no tool-count guidance: the function-calling docs (https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/function_calling/, tier 1, checked 2026-08-19) list Mistral Medium 3.5 among the function-calling models but state no maximum or recommended number of tools and no degradation threshold. Binding limits that DO apply: the documented 128-tool hard cap per request (see max_tools_hard, https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations, tier 1) and the 256,000-token shared input+output context window that every tool definition is billed into. Any cross-vendor 10-20-tool rule of thumb applied to Mistral is an unmeasured extrapolation, not a Mistral measurement.

tool_definition_shape.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19: {"type": "function", "function": {name, description, parameters}} with a JSON-Schema `parameters` object — identical in shape to OpenAI function calling. tool_choice accepts auto (default) | any/required | none | a named tool.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19: Known Limitations states that tool descriptions consume tokens from the available context. Tool definitions are therefore billed as input tokens and eat the same 256k window as the messages — the premise of the footprint measurement.

tool_search_deferral.notes: Still no automatic/lazy tool loading: nothing in the API defers tool schemas or lets the model search a catalog. What exists as of 2026-08-19 is manual, human-side pruning — admins can 'turn individual tools on or off for a whole org or one workspace' inside a Connector, Vibe Code offers a `/connectors` picker to choose which tools to enable, and the Vibe CLI supports enabled_tools/disabled_tools glob or regex filters (https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/mcp-servers). Those shrink what is sent, but every surviving tool is still serialized into every request.

max_tool_name_len.notes: No character ceiling or pattern for function/tool names is published: the API reference documents the `tools` parameter but not a Function object schema with maxLength/pattern (checked 2026-08-19). Two adjacent caps that DO bind: Connector (MCP server registry) names are 'up to 64 characters, alphanumeric with underscores and dashes only' (https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/connectors/management), and the Vibe CLI namespaces MCP tools as {server_name}_{tool_name} (https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/mcp-servers), so a long server alias eats into whatever name budget the model-side parser has.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No character or token ceiling for a tool description is published (re-checked 2026-08-19). The binding constraint is budgetary, not syntactic: Known Limitations says descriptions consume tokens from the available context, so long descriptions across 128 tools are charged against the shared 256k window.

max_request_size.notes: No byte/MB payload ceiling is documented for POST /v1/chat/completions (the chat endpoint reference documents no array or payload size limits, checked 2026-08-19). Adjacent caps that are documented and that DO bind on neighbouring paths: 512 MB per uploaded file, 512 MB per batch file with up to 100,000 requests, 20 MB per image, 500 MB / 60 minutes per audio file. For chat itself the binding ceilings are the 256k token window and the 128-tool aggregate cap.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No numeric size ceiling for an individual tool result is documented (checked 2026-08-19). A tool result is an ordinary `tool`-role message, so it is charged against the shared 256k input+output window — that window, not a size rule, is what a chatty MCP tool blows.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: parallel_tool_calls is a boolean (default true) — no numeric ceiling on how many tool calls the model may emit in one turn is published (re-checked on the chat endpoint reference 2026-08-19). The 128-tool aggregate cap limits what is offered, not how many are invoked at once.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No numeric ceiling on tool-call/result cycles per turn or per agentic loop is published; the function calling guide's worked example loops back to the model until it produces a final answer without stating a cycle ceiling (re-checked 2026-08-19). Cost and the 256k window are what bound a long agentic run.

max_connected_servers.notes: No numeric ceiling on the number of Connectors (MCP servers) per workspace, org, agent or conversation is published (Connectors API reference and management docs re-checked 2026-08-19); listing uses keyset pagination with a page_size shown as high as 1000, which implies large counts are expected. Mistral advertises 'more than 60 integrations' plus custom MCP connectors (https://mistral.ai/news/more-control-over-connectors/). The limit that actually binds when you attach many servers is the aggregate 128-tool per-request cap.

max_total_tools.notes: No separate aggregate catalog ceiling exists above the per-request cap: on Mistral the aggregate cap IS max_tools_hard = 128 tools per request, summed across your own functions, every connected Connector's tools and the built-in tools. GET /v1/connectors/{id}/tools paginates (default page_size 100) with no documented maximum tool count per connector (https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/connectors/management).

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Re-checked 2026-08-19. Connector (MCP server registry) names: 'up to 64 characters, alphanumeric with underscores and dashes only', unique within a workspace (https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/connectors/management / https://docs.mistral.ai/api/endpoint/beta/connectors). Tool function name cap: not published — the API reference documents the `tools` parameter but no Function object maxLength/pattern (https://docs.mistral.ai/api). No documented limit on JSON-Schema nesting depth, property count, enum size, or on unsupported keywords such as oneOf/anyOf/$ref — Mistral publishes no schema-shape rules at all, so the only reliable ceiling is the token budget: tool descriptions and schemas are charged as input against the shared 256k window (https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations). Vibe CLI namespaces MCP tools as {server_name}_{tool_name} (https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/mcp-servers).
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-19 — rate limits are set at the ORGANIZATION level and apply across all workspaces (the 2026-06-21 entry said 'per API key', which the tier docs contradict); three independent limits are enforced: requests per second, tokens per minute and tokens per month, with tier upgrades driven by cumulative billed amount and the actual numbers only visible in Admin > Limits (https://docs.mistral.ai/deployment/ai-studio/tier). Batch processing is 50% cheaper and does not compete with real-time limits; max batch file 512 MB / 100,000 requests, results retained 24h; streaming connections drop after 10 minutes of inactivity (https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations). Prompt caching is now documented and is EXPLICIT, not automatic: pass prompt_cache_key, cache blocks are 64 tokens so cached_tokens is always a multiple of 64 and prompts under 64 tokens never hit, and cached prompt tokens bill at 10% of the standard input price (https://docs.mistral.ai/studio-api/conversations/advanced/prompt-caching). Connectors remain Public Preview; connector tool schemas are serialized into the request, so a large MCP server consumes a real share of the 256k window and of the 128-tool aggregate cap. Regional endpoints (EU/US) are GA and a Priority Tier with custom rate limits and an uptime SLA is in public preview (https://mistral.ai/news/regional-inference-open-models-new-compute/).

strict_function_schema.notes: Re-checked 2026-08-19: Mistral documents no OpenAI-style `strict` flag and no structural schema restrictions (no 100-property / 5-level-depth / no-oneOf rules). The function calling guide exposes only name/description/parameters plus tool_choice and parallel_tool_calls. Structured Outputs is a separate response-format feature, not a tool schema mode.

skills_supported.notes: Upgraded sourcing 2026-08-19: Mistral now has a literal Skills primitive (Studio and Vibe), announced 2026-07-09, in addition to Agents. A Skill packages 'a reusable method, checklist, or procedure that an AI assistant can apply when a task matches', with a trigger description, instructions and optional attached files, and Studio versions it immutably with rollback.

skills_loading_model.notes: CHANGED always_on -> progressive_disclosure. Vibe documents a three-stage load: at session start 'Work loads only each Skill's name and description (~100 tokens each)'; when a task matches the description the full SKILL.md loads into context; referenced supporting files load only as needed. Studio says the same in prose — 'the description field ... determines when the assistant loads the Skill' (https://docs.mistral.ai/getting-started/quickstarts/studio/create-skill). NOTE the asymmetry that matters for footprinting: Skills are progressively disclosed, but MCP/Connector TOOL definitions are not — those are serialized into every request.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: Re-measured against the docs 2026-08-19. Skills: ~100 tokens per enabled Skill at discovery (name + description only), then the full SKILL.md on activation, then referenced files on demand (https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/work/skills); Mistral publishes no size ceiling for SKILL.md and only an unquantified 'supporting files are subject to a file-count limit'. Agents: the agent's `instructions` and its tool list are fixed at creation and injected into the conversation, billed as input tokens. Connector (MCP) tool schemas are NOT progressively disclosed — every tool left enabled is serialized into every request and charged as input (https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations). Prompt caching can recover 90% of the cost of that repeated prefix if a stable prompt_cache_key is supplied (https://docs.mistral.ai/studio-api/conversations/advanced/prompt-caching).
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: No fixed platform-injected system prompt is documented (checked 2026-08-19). Overhead is developer-controlled through the agent's `instructions` field (https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/agents/introduction) plus whichever Skills are enabled (~100 tokens each until activated) and whichever tool definitions are attached, all of which are billed as input against the shared 256k window.

prompt_caching.notes: CHANGED false -> true. Prompt caching is documented as of 2026-08-19 and is explicit: set prompt_cache_key to 'a stable application-level identifier, such as a conversation ID, session ID, or workflow ID'. Cache blocks are 64 tokens, so cached_tokens is always a multiple of 64 and 'prompts with fewer than 64 prompt tokens do not have cache hits'; supplying the key 'doesn't guarantee' a hit. Cached prompt tokens bill at 10% of the standard input price. TTL is not published, nor is whether tool definitions specifically are cacheable — only that a compatible cached PREFIX is matched, which a stable tools array at the head of the request should satisfy.

memory_feature.notes: Agents documentation describes 'persistent state across conversations' and agent-to-agent handoffs (re-checked 2026-08-19). Server-side conversation history is replayed as input tokens on each continuation, so a long session's context — and cost — grows turn over turn. The exact `store` parameter semantics are no longer spelled out on the current Agents introduction page.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Re-verified against the API pricing table and the model card 2026-08-19; unchanged.

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Re-verified against the API pricing table and the model card 2026-08-19; unchanged.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: CHANGED null -> 0.15. DERIVED: prompt caching now exists and 'cached prompt tokens are billed at 10% of the standard input token price', so this is 10% of the 1.5 USD/1M input rate. Mistral does not print a per-model cached rate on the pricing page (the marketing page phrases it as 'cached input tokens reduce input cost by up to 90%', https://mistral.ai/pricing), hence confidence medium rather than high.

batch_discount.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19: 'Batch processing, for high-volume work, reduces the price by 50%'. Batch does not compete with real-time rate limits; max batch file 512 MB / 100,000 requests (https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations).

billing_unit.notes: Priced per million input and output tokens, counted separately.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Checked 2026-08-19: no per-image or per-tile token rule and no per-image surcharge is published — the Vision page leaves 'How many tokens correspond to an image' as an unanswered FAQ heading (https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/vision); images are simply capped at 20 MB each (https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations). Audio is not a capability of this model; transcription/TTS run on the separate Voxtral models and endpoints and are priced separately (https://mistral.ai/pricing/api).

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: Left null deliberately. The model does emit thinking content when reasoning_effort='high' (a ThinkChunk precedes the TextChunk), and Mistral warns it means 'increased token usage', but no page states which meter those tokens land on or exposes a separate reasoning-token price or budget. Assume output-priced for planning, but that is not documented.

models.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19; still Mistral's flagship general-purpose model and unchanged since the 2026-06-21 capture (no successor shipped — the only model releases between 2026-06-21 and today were OCR 4.0 on 2026-06-23, Leanstral 1.5 on 2026-06-30 and OCR 4.1 on 2026-07-16, none of them generalist). API string mistral-medium-3-5-26-04 (alias mistral-medium-latest); v26.04, released 2026-04-28, Modified MIT open weights. The official HF card corrects two things in the previous entry: it is a DENSE 128B model (not MoE), it takes text+image in and emits text only (no audio), and it exposes a per-request reasoning_effort of 'none' or 'high'. 256k context, 128-tool aggregate cap, $1.5/$7.5 per 1M in/out — all unchanged.

It is not a per-MCP-server cap; no per-server tool cap is documented anywhere.

max_tools_practical.notes: CHANGED 20 → null (2026-08-19 final audit): no empirical source has measured a Mistral model's tool-count degradation, so no practical tool ceiling can be asserted for Mistral Small 4. The previously cited leaderboard (https://presenc.ai/research/ai-agent-tool-calling-accuracy-benchmarks-2026, tier 4, re-opened 2026-08-19) measures only Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-5, Qwen 3 235B, Llama 4 405B, Qwen 3 32B, Llama 4 70B and DeepSeek V4 — NO Mistral model appears in it, so its "accuracy degrades to 85-91 percent at 5 tools, then to 65-78 percent at 20+ tools" band (exemplified on Claude Opus 4.7: 96% at 1 tool → 91% at 5 → 76% at 20+) is evidence about those models only. The practitioner write-up previously quoted alongside it (https://tianpan.co/blog/2026-04-19-over-tooled-agent-problem, "safe zone ... at roughly 10-20 tools per reasoning context") likewise names no Mistral model. Mistral itself publishes no tool-count guidance: the function-calling docs (https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/function_calling/, tier 1, checked 2026-08-19) list Mistral Small 4 among the function-calling models but state no maximum or recommended number of tools and no degradation threshold. Binding limits that DO apply: the documented 128-tool hard cap per request (see max_tools_hard, https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations, tier 1) and the 256,000-token shared input+output context window that every tool definition is billed into. Any cross-vendor 10-20-tool rule of thumb applied to Mistral is an unmeasured extrapolation, not a Mistral measurement.

tool_definition_shape.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19: {"type": "function", "function": {name, description, parameters}} with a JSON-Schema `parameters` object — identical in shape to OpenAI function calling. tool_choice accepts auto (default) | any/required | none | a named tool.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19: Known Limitations states that tool descriptions consume tokens from the available context. Tool definitions are therefore billed as input tokens and eat the same 256k window as the messages — the premise of the footprint measurement.

tool_search_deferral.notes: Still no automatic/lazy tool loading: nothing in the API defers tool schemas or lets the model search a catalog. What exists as of 2026-08-19 is manual, human-side pruning — admins can 'turn individual tools on or off for a whole org or one workspace' inside a Connector, Vibe Code offers a `/connectors` picker to choose which tools to enable, and the Vibe CLI supports enabled_tools/disabled_tools glob or regex filters (https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/mcp-servers). Those shrink what is sent, but every surviving tool is still serialized into every request.

max_tool_name_len.notes: No character ceiling or pattern for function/tool names is published: the API reference documents the `tools` parameter but not a Function object schema with maxLength/pattern (checked 2026-08-19). Two adjacent caps that DO bind: Connector (MCP server registry) names are 'up to 64 characters, alphanumeric with underscores and dashes only' (https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/connectors/management), and the Vibe CLI namespaces MCP tools as {server_name}_{tool_name} (https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/mcp-servers), so a long server alias eats into whatever name budget the model-side parser has.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No character or token ceiling for a tool description is published (re-checked 2026-08-19). The binding constraint is budgetary, not syntactic: Known Limitations says descriptions consume tokens from the available context, so long descriptions across 128 tools are charged against the shared 256k window.

max_request_size.notes: No byte/MB payload ceiling is documented for POST /v1/chat/completions (the chat endpoint reference documents no array or payload size limits, checked 2026-08-19). Adjacent caps that are documented and that DO bind on neighbouring paths: 512 MB per uploaded file, 512 MB per batch file with up to 100,000 requests, 20 MB per image, 500 MB / 60 minutes per audio file. For chat itself the binding ceilings are the 256k token window and the 128-tool aggregate cap.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No numeric size ceiling for an individual tool result is documented (checked 2026-08-19). A tool result is an ordinary `tool`-role message, so it is charged against the shared 256k input+output window — that window, not a size rule, is what a chatty MCP tool blows.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: parallel_tool_calls is a boolean (default true) — no numeric ceiling on how many tool calls the model may emit in one turn is published (re-checked on the chat endpoint reference 2026-08-19). The 128-tool aggregate cap limits what is offered, not how many are invoked at once.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No numeric ceiling on tool-call/result cycles per turn or per agentic loop is published; the function calling guide's worked example loops back to the model until it produces a final answer without stating a cycle ceiling (re-checked 2026-08-19). Cost and the 256k window are what bound a long agentic run.

max_connected_servers.notes: No numeric ceiling on the number of Connectors (MCP servers) per workspace, org, agent or conversation is published (Connectors API reference and management docs re-checked 2026-08-19); listing uses keyset pagination with a page_size shown as high as 1000, which implies large counts are expected. Mistral advertises 'more than 60 integrations' plus custom MCP connectors (https://mistral.ai/news/more-control-over-connectors/). The limit that actually binds when you attach many servers is the aggregate 128-tool per-request cap.

max_total_tools.notes: No separate aggregate catalog ceiling exists above the per-request cap: on Mistral the aggregate cap IS max_tools_hard = 128 tools per request, summed across your own functions, every connected Connector's tools and the built-in tools. GET /v1/connectors/{id}/tools paginates (default page_size 100) with no documented maximum tool count per connector (https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/connectors/management).

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Re-checked 2026-08-19. Connector (MCP server registry) names: 'up to 64 characters, alphanumeric with underscores and dashes only', unique within a workspace (https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/connectors/management / https://docs.mistral.ai/api/endpoint/beta/connectors). Tool function name cap: not published — the API reference documents the `tools` parameter but no Function object maxLength/pattern (https://docs.mistral.ai/api). No documented limit on JSON-Schema nesting depth, property count, enum size, or on unsupported keywords such as oneOf/anyOf/$ref — Mistral publishes no schema-shape rules at all, so the only reliable ceiling is the token budget: tool descriptions and schemas are charged as input against the shared 256k window (https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations). Vibe CLI namespaces MCP tools as {server_name}_{tool_name} (https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/mcp-servers).
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-19 — rate limits are set at the ORGANIZATION level and apply across all workspaces (the 2026-06-21 entry said 'per API key', which the tier docs contradict); three independent limits are enforced: requests per second, tokens per minute and tokens per month, with tier upgrades driven by cumulative billed amount and the actual numbers only visible in Admin > Limits (https://docs.mistral.ai/deployment/ai-studio/tier). Batch processing is 50% cheaper and does not compete with real-time limits; max batch file 512 MB / 100,000 requests, results retained 24h; streaming connections drop after 10 minutes of inactivity (https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations). Prompt caching is now documented and is EXPLICIT, not automatic: pass prompt_cache_key, cache blocks are 64 tokens so cached_tokens is always a multiple of 64 and prompts under 64 tokens never hit, and cached prompt tokens bill at 10% of the standard input price (https://docs.mistral.ai/studio-api/conversations/advanced/prompt-caching). Connectors remain Public Preview; connector tool schemas are serialized into the request, so a large MCP server consumes a real share of the 256k window and of the 128-tool aggregate cap. Regional endpoints (EU/US) are GA and a Priority Tier with custom rate limits and an uptime SLA is in public preview (https://mistral.ai/news/regional-inference-open-models-new-compute/).

strict_function_schema.notes: Re-checked 2026-08-19: Mistral documents no OpenAI-style `strict` flag and no structural schema restrictions (no 100-property / 5-level-depth / no-oneOf rules). The function calling guide exposes only name/description/parameters plus tool_choice and parallel_tool_calls. Structured Outputs is a separate response-format feature, not a tool schema mode.

skills_supported.notes: Upgraded sourcing 2026-08-19: Mistral now has a literal Skills primitive (Studio and Vibe), announced 2026-07-09, in addition to Agents. A Skill packages 'a reusable method, checklist, or procedure that an AI assistant can apply when a task matches', with a trigger description, instructions and optional attached files, and Studio versions it immutably with rollback.

skills_loading_model.notes: CHANGED always_on -> progressive_disclosure. Vibe documents a three-stage load: at session start 'Work loads only each Skill's name and description (~100 tokens each)'; when a task matches the description the full SKILL.md loads into context; referenced supporting files load only as needed. Studio says the same in prose — 'the description field ... determines when the assistant loads the Skill' (https://docs.mistral.ai/getting-started/quickstarts/studio/create-skill). NOTE the asymmetry that matters for footprinting: Skills are progressively disclosed, but MCP/Connector TOOL definitions are not — those are serialized into every request.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: Re-measured against the docs 2026-08-19. Skills: ~100 tokens per enabled Skill at discovery (name + description only), then the full SKILL.md on activation, then referenced files on demand (https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/work/skills); Mistral publishes no size ceiling for SKILL.md and only an unquantified 'supporting files are subject to a file-count limit'. Agents: the agent's `instructions` and its tool list are fixed at creation and injected into the conversation, billed as input tokens. Connector (MCP) tool schemas are NOT progressively disclosed — every tool left enabled is serialized into every request and charged as input (https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations). Prompt caching can recover 90% of the cost of that repeated prefix if a stable prompt_cache_key is supplied (https://docs.mistral.ai/studio-api/conversations/advanced/prompt-caching).
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: No fixed platform-injected system prompt is documented (checked 2026-08-19). Overhead is developer-controlled through the agent's `instructions` field (https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/agents/introduction) plus whichever Skills are enabled (~100 tokens each until activated) and whichever tool definitions are attached, all of which are billed as input against the shared 256k window.

prompt_caching.notes: CHANGED false -> true. Prompt caching is documented as of 2026-08-19 and is explicit: set prompt_cache_key to 'a stable application-level identifier, such as a conversation ID, session ID, or workflow ID'. Cache blocks are 64 tokens, so cached_tokens is always a multiple of 64 and 'prompts with fewer than 64 prompt tokens do not have cache hits'; supplying the key 'doesn't guarantee' a hit. Cached prompt tokens bill at 10% of the standard input price. TTL is not published, nor is whether tool definitions specifically are cacheable — only that a compatible cached PREFIX is matched, which a stable tools array at the head of the request should satisfy.

memory_feature.notes: Agents documentation describes 'persistent state across conversations' and agent-to-agent handoffs (re-checked 2026-08-19). Server-side conversation history is replayed as input tokens on each continuation, so a long session's context — and cost — grows turn over turn. The exact `store` parameter semantics are no longer spelled out on the current Agents introduction page.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Re-verified against the API pricing table and the model card 2026-08-19; unchanged.

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Re-verified against the API pricing table and the model card 2026-08-19; unchanged.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: CHANGED null -> 0.015. DERIVED: prompt caching now exists and 'cached prompt tokens are billed at 10% of the standard input token price', so this is 10% of the 0.15 USD/1M input rate. Mistral does not print a per-model cached rate on the pricing page (the marketing page phrases it as 'cached input tokens reduce input cost by up to 90%', https://mistral.ai/pricing), hence confidence medium rather than high.

batch_discount.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19: 'Batch processing, for high-volume work, reduces the price by 50%'. Batch does not compete with real-time rate limits; max batch file 512 MB / 100,000 requests (https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations).

billing_unit.notes: Priced per million input and output tokens, counted separately.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Checked 2026-08-19: no per-image or per-tile token rule and no per-image surcharge is published — the Vision page leaves 'How many tokens correspond to an image' as an unanswered FAQ heading (https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/vision); images are simply capped at 20 MB each (https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations). Audio is not a capability of this model; transcription/TTS run on the separate Voxtral models and endpoints and are priced separately (https://mistral.ai/pricing/api).

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: Left null deliberately. The model does emit thinking content when reasoning_effort='high' (a ThinkChunk precedes the TextChunk), and Mistral warns it means 'increased token usage', but no page states which meter those tokens land on or exposes a separate reasoning-token price or budget. Assume output-priced for planning, but that is not documented.

models.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19; unchanged. API string mistral-small-2603 (alias mistral-small-latest); v26.03, released 2026-03-16, Apache 2.0. 119B total / 6.5B active MoE (128 experts, 4 active per the official HF card), hybrid instruct+reasoning+coding, text+image in / text out, per-request reasoning_effort none|high. 256k context, 128-tool aggregate cap, $0.15/$0.60 per 1M in/out. Not affected by any announced deprecation — the retirements in flight cover Mistral Small 3.2 (2026-07-31) and Mistral Medium 3 / 3.1 (2026-08-31).

release_date.notes: Re-verified on the model card 2026-08-19; unchanged.

knowledge_cutoff.notes: Still not published. Checked the Mistral model card (https://docs.mistral.ai/models/model-cards/mistral-large-3-25-12) and the official Hugging Face model card (https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-3) on 2026-08-19 — neither states a training-data cutoff date.

context_window_tokens.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19: the Known Limitations context-window table still lists this model at 256k tokens; the official HF model card (https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-3) repeats '256k context'.

input_output_shared.notes: Known Limitations, re-read 2026-08-19: both input and output tokens are included in the context calculation — 'Plan your max_tokens accordingly.'

max_input_tokens.notes: No separate input ceiling is published. The chat endpoint reference states only that 'The token count of your prompt plus max_tokens cannot exceed the model's context length', so the effective input ceiling is 256k minus the requested max_tokens. Not recorded as a number because it is request-dependent, not a documented constant.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: No default value for max_tokens is documented on the chat endpoint reference (re-read 2026-08-19); the parameter is described without a stated default or maximum.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: No per-completion output ceiling is published. The only documented bound is 'prompt + max_tokens cannot exceed the model's context length' (256k). This is a genuine documentation gap, not an absence of constraint — the shared 256k window is what binds.

extended_context.notes: No extended/beta context tier beyond 256k appears in the Known Limitations table (re-read 2026-08-19).

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Mistral Large 3 is not listed among the models that accept reasoning_effort on the Reasoning page (only mistral-small-latest and mistral-medium-3-5 are, checked 2026-08-19), so no reasoning-token accounting applies.

tokenizer_family.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19. Mistral's tokenization deep-dive still documents V1/V2/V3 with V3-Tekken as the tiktoken-based variant used by recent models; the official HF card for this model (https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-3) names Tekken and pins a minimum mistral-common version. Exact Tekken sub-version per model is not published.

tokenizer_public.notes: mistral-common remains open source; tokenizer files are downloadable from the HF Hub.

tokenizer_access.value: pip install mistral-common; MistralTokenizer.from_hf_hub("<hf-model-id>") pulls the Tekken tokenizer from the HF Hub
tokenizer_access.notes: Refreshed 2026-08-19 to the current documented loading path. Extras: pip install "mistral-common[image]" / "mistral-common[audio,hf-hub]".

count_tokens_method.value: from mistral_common.tokens.tokenizers.mistral import MistralTokenizer; tok = MistralTokenizer.from_hf_hub("<hf-model-id>"); n = len(tok.encode_chat_completion(ChatCompletionRequest(messages=[...])).tokens)
count_tokens_method.notes: CHANGED: the previously recorded MistralTokenizer.v3() call is superseded by the documented from_hf_hub + encode_chat_completion flow. Caveat verified 2026-08-19: the mistral-common usage docs show no worked example of putting `tools` into the ChatCompletionRequest, so tool-definition token counts obtained this way are reconstructions, not a vendor-blessed recipe. Mistral exposes no server-side count-tokens endpoint.

image_token_rule.notes: Still undocumented, and now confirmed as a deliberate gap: the Vision capability page carries the FAQ heading 'How many tokens correspond to an image and/or what is the maximum resolution?' with no answer beneath it (checked 2026-08-19). The only published image constraint is a 20 MB per-image cap in Known Limitations (https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations).

audio_token_rule.notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-19: the model card does not list audio as a capability for this model, and the official HF card (https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-3) gives the modalities as text+image in / text out. Audio is handled by the separate Voxtral models and endpoints, so no audio token rule applies here. (The 2026-06-21 entry's 'audio transcription listed as a feature' claim did not hold up on re-read.)

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: CHANGED to null: the previous 4.0 was an unsourced industry rule of thumb. Searched Mistral's tokenization deep-dive, the mistral-common docs and the Tekken tokenizer card (https://huggingface.co/toksuite/mistralai-tekken, vocab 130,000, tier 3) on 2026-08-19 — no chars-per-token or bytes-per-token figure is published for Tekken. The only quantitative claim Mistral makes is relative: Tekken is '~30% more efficient at compressing source code, Chinese, Italian, French, German, Spanish, and Russian' and 2x/3x on Korean/Arabic versus the Llama 3 tokenizer. Use mistral-common for exact counts.

function_calling.notes: Function Calling is listed in the model card's feature list (re-verified 2026-08-19) and the model appears in the function-calling guide's supported-model list (https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/function_calling).

native_mcp.notes: Platform-level: any function-calling model can be pointed at registered Connectors (MCP servers), whose tools the model 'discovers automatically and calls ... based on the user's request'. Still Public Preview as of 2026-08-19; the API interface can change. Vibe Code additionally speaks MCP directly over stdio, HTTP and streamable HTTP (https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/mcp-servers).

parallel_tool_calls.notes: Re-verified on the chat endpoint reference 2026-08-19: parallel_tool_calls — 'Whether to enable parallel function calling during tool use, when enabled the model can call multiple tools in parallel.' Default Value: true.

The function calling guide exposes only name/description/parameters plus tool_choice and parallel_tool_calls. Structured Outputs is a separate response-format feature, not a tool schema mode.

skills_supported.notes: Upgraded sourcing 2026-08-19: Mistral now has a literal Skills primitive (Studio and Vibe), announced 2026-07-09, in addition to Agents. A Skill packages 'a reusable method, checklist, or procedure that an AI assistant can apply when a task matches', with a trigger description, instructions and optional attached files, and Studio versions it immutably with rollback.

skills_loading_model.notes: CHANGED always_on -> progressive_disclosure. Vibe documents a three-stage load: at session start 'Work loads only each Skill's name and description (~100 tokens each)'; when a task matches the description the full SKILL.md loads into context; referenced supporting files load only as needed. Studio says the same in prose — 'the description field ... determines when the assistant loads the Skill' (https://docs.mistral.ai/getting-started/quickstarts/studio/create-skill). NOTE the asymmetry that matters for footprinting: Skills are progressively disclosed, but MCP/Connector TOOL definitions are not — those are serialized into every request.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: Re-measured against the docs 2026-08-19. Skills: ~100 tokens per enabled Skill at discovery (name + description only), then the full SKILL.md on activation, then referenced files on demand (https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/work/skills); Mistral publishes no size ceiling for SKILL.md and only an unquantified 'supporting files are subject to a file-count limit'. Agents: the agent's `instructions` and its tool list are fixed at creation and injected into the conversation, billed as input tokens. Connector (MCP) tool schemas are NOT progressively disclosed — every tool left enabled is serialized into every request and charged as input (https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations). Prompt caching can recover 90% of the cost of that repeated prefix if a stable prompt_cache_key is supplied (https://docs.mistral.ai/studio-api/conversations/advanced/prompt-caching).
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: No fixed platform-injected system prompt is documented (checked 2026-08-19). Overhead is developer-controlled through the agent's `instructions` field (https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/agents/introduction) plus whichever Skills are enabled (~100 tokens each until activated) and whichever tool definitions are attached, all of which are billed as input against the shared 256k window.

prompt_caching.notes: CHANGED false -> true. Prompt caching is documented as of 2026-08-19 and is explicit: set prompt_cache_key to 'a stable application-level identifier, such as a conversation ID, session ID, or workflow ID'. Cache blocks are 64 tokens, so cached_tokens is always a multiple of 64 and 'prompts with fewer than 64 prompt tokens do not have cache hits'; supplying the key 'doesn't guarantee' a hit. Cached prompt tokens bill at 10% of the standard input price. TTL is not published, nor is whether tool definitions specifically are cacheable — only that a compatible cached PREFIX is matched, which a stable tools array at the head of the request should satisfy.

memory_feature.notes: Agents documentation describes 'persistent state across conversations' and agent-to-agent handoffs (re-checked 2026-08-19). Server-side conversation history is replayed as input tokens on each continuation, so a long session's context — and cost — grows turn over turn. The exact `store` parameter semantics are no longer spelled out on the current Agents introduction page.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Re-verified against the API pricing table and the model card 2026-08-19; unchanged.

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Re-verified against the API pricing table and the model card 2026-08-19; unchanged.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: CHANGED null -> 0.05. DERIVED: prompt caching now exists and 'cached prompt tokens are billed at 10% of the standard input token price', so this is 10% of the 0.5 USD/1M input rate. Mistral does not print a per-model cached rate on the pricing page (the marketing page phrases it as 'cached input tokens reduce input cost by up to 90%', https://mistral.ai/pricing), hence confidence medium rather than high.

batch_discount.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19: 'Batch processing, for high-volume work, reduces the price by 50%'. Batch does not compete with real-time rate limits; max batch file 512 MB / 100,000 requests (https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations).

billing_unit.notes: Priced per million input and output tokens, counted separately.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Checked 2026-08-19: no per-image or per-tile token rule and no per-image surcharge is published — the Vision page leaves 'How many tokens correspond to an image' as an unanswered FAQ heading (https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/vision); images are simply capped at 20 MB each (https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations). Audio is not a capability of this model; transcription/TTS run on the separate Voxtral models and endpoints and are priced separately (https://mistral.ai/pricing/api).

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: Not a reasoning model — Mistral Large 3 is not listed among the models accepting reasoning_effort (checked 2026-08-19), so no reasoning-token billing arises.

models.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19; unchanged. API string mistral-large-2512 (alias mistral-large-latest); v25.12, released 2025-12-02. CORRECTION to the previous entry: the licence is Apache 2.0, not Modified MIT (both the model card and the official HF card say Apache 2.0). 675B total / 41B active granular MoE including a 2.5B vision encoder, 256k context, $0.5/$1.5 per 1M in/out. Not a reasoning model — it is absent from the reasoning_effort model list. Despite being the oldest of the three it is still listed as a current generalist model on the models overview, so status stays ga.
